stem:
Qadir looks at a clear drop of pond water. With his unaided eyes he sees nothing moving in it. His teacher says the tiniest living organisms may still be present. He considers a microscope, an ordinary magnifying glass, his unaided eyes again, or a flat windowpane.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: He should use a microscope, because those organisms are too small for the unaided eye.
An ordinary magnifying glass is enough to see the tiniest organisms clearly.
His unaided eyes are enough, because clear pond water has nothing tiny to observe.
A flat windowpane will magnify them, because any clear glass makes small things look larger.

teacher.key_rationale: Tiny organisms in the drop need a microscope because they are below the unaided eye's size limit. An ordinary magnifying glass is not enough for the tiniest detail; clear water does not mean nothing is there; flat clear glass does not magnify.

mx_swap.reason: Adult-butterfly CWO invents a butterfly not in the stem; kept term_substitution, condition_omission, and surface_feature_capture on the pond-drop hinge.
